remaining_concerns: No genuinely new admissible evidence was added; the Actor mainly reframed the same record more narrowly.
BPROC-036-C and BPROC-036-D show diligence gaps and inconsistency, but the policy text says those facts by themselves justify follow-up or escalation, not reject-level proof.
BPROC-036-E supports a conditional 'follow-up before approval if unresolved' position more directly than it supports rejection as the compliant disposition.
The admissible record still does not clearly establish that the cited storage-control concern remained materially unresolved at the exact decision point under a documented rejection threshold.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. The revised argument is materially narrower and more careful, but it remains a reinterpretation of BPROC-036-C through BPROC-036-E rather than new proof. That narrowing matters: it removes the overstatement that the file proves an actual control failure. But the remaining compliance predicate is still unresolved. Under the policy, vendor rejection must rest on admissible due-diligence evidence showing a material unresolved risk, while quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies alone support follow-up or escalation. BPROC-036-E documents a follow-up-before-approval condition if storage controls remain unresolved; it does not itself show that the unresolved condition persisted at the decision point or that rejection, rather than further diligence or escalation, was the supported outcome. That makes the rejection rationale still inadequately supported on the present record, even if the Actor's caveated framing is more defensible than the original broader claim.
